newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Worried EU may send Irish Minister to Mideast talks.
newsitem.headline: Worried EU may send Irish Minister to Mideast talks.

text.p: European Union leaders, sidelined in a U.S.-led attempt to revive the Middle East peace process, may send Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring to attend Israeli-Palestinian talks on Sunday, EU officials said.

They said the crisis in the Middle East peace process dominated much of the early part of a one-day EU Dublin summit and a decision to send Spring, whose country is current EU President, could be announced later in the day.

Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat appealed this week for EU involvement in efforts to rebuild the peace process after negotiations with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ended inconclusively in the United States.
The officials said letters to Arafat, Netanyahu and U.S. President Bill Clinton appealing for renewed efforts to negotiate an end to violence were also being considered.
Israel and the Palestinian Authority hold talks on the Israeli border on Sunday. The discussions were the main result of U.S.-brokered talks on Tuesday.
Both sides are expected to discuss the closure of an archeological tunnel in Arab East Jerusalem whose opening sparked violence which killed 73 people.
A potentially controversial fact-finding visit to the region by a "troika" of EU ministers could also take place in the next 10 days, EU diplomats said.
They said ministers from Ireland, Italy and Netherlands had pencilled in the middle of October to meet Palestinian leaders in their Orient House offices in disputed East Jerusalem.

The Israeli government has already signalled that it would strongly disapprove of any visit by the EU troika to Orient House, which it would see as backing for Palestinian claims to the disputed city.
It has raised the possibility that it would not meet the troika if it went to Orient House.
"It's not inconceivable that the troika would go to Orient House and not hold talks with the Israelis. We'll just have to see," said one EU diplomat close to the discussions.
"But the middle of the month, October 15 to 18, is the sort of date we are looking at. There is some urgency," he said.

The leaders of France and Italy are pressing the summit to reaffirm Europe's desire to play a role in rescuing the Middle East peace process, which has been dominated by the mediation efforts of Clinton's administration.
"There are one or two delegations at the summit who very keenly want the EU to be involved in this process," said one EU diplomat. "I expect they will make their views known."

Arafat has held separate talks with Italy's Prime Minister, Romano Prodi, and French President Jacques Chirac, to press for EU involvement and brief them on his Washington talks this week with Netanyahu.

The EU agreed in July that Orient House should be the venue for talks with leaders of the Palestinian Authority but was told by Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy that the body no longer held official meetings there.

EU Foreign Ministers said last month that they would seek clarification on the Israeli claim from the Palestinian Authority and were told that Orient House was still being used by Palestinians as a political office.
Spring paid a visit to Palestine Liberation Organisation officials at Orient House in 1995 and was promptly snubbed by the Israeli President, who cancelled planned talks.
